title: Translate virtual addresses with base and bounds, then with segments
brief: Build the check-and-add that gives every process its own address space, then split the space into code, heap, and a stack that grows down.
hints: Base and bounds is two lines: if not 0 <= vaddr < bounds, raise SegmentationFault; otherwise return base + vaddr.
With a 14-bit address, the top 2 bits pick the segment and the low 12 bits are the offset: vaddr >> 12 and vaddr & 0xFFF. Anything outside 0..16383 is a fault.
For a segment that grows up, fault if offset >= size and return base + offset.

For the stack, base is the physical address just past its top byte. Compute back = SEG_SIZE - offset (how far below the top the byte sits). Fault if back > size, otherwise the physical address is base - back.
Check the write permission before translating: a write to a segment with writable=False raises SegmentationFault, even when the address is inside the segment.
relocate copies the bytes first (bytes(mem[lo:hi])) and then writes them, so overlapping source and destination are safe. Validate that the whole new range sits inside mem before you copy anything.
